name: Joiakim
overview: Joiakim was a male Levite known primarily as the son of Jeshua and the father of Eliashib, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:10. His exact identity among the Jeshuas mentioned in Scripture is uncertain, as he could be the son of Jeshua_5, Jeshua_7, or Jeshua_8, all of whom were Levites. This places Joiakim within the priestly tribe of Levi, emphasizing his role in the Levitical lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Joiakim means 'YHWH lifts up,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning centered on God's uplifting power. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant spiritual implications consistent with Levitical heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Joiakim as the son of Jeshua and the father of Eliashib, establishing a clear generational link within the Levitical line. No additional family relationships are documented beyond these connections in Nehemiah 12:10.
scriptureSignificance: Joiakim's significance lies in his placement within the priestly genealogy, linking Jeshua and Eliashib, both notable Levites. This connection underscores the continuity of priestly service and the faithful transmission of Levitical duties in the post-exilic community. His mention in Nehemiah highlights the importance of preserving genealogical records to affirm identity and heritage among God's people.
